svg.title: The extra scalar block at the finite path cutoff
svg.desc: For r at least four, lambda is one over four cosine squared pi over r. Compression recognizes the basic-construction part of B. A scalar common-kernel block s is allowed in B. The canonical new scalar block exists for k at most r minus four, disappears at k equals r minus three, and the old projection join forces s zero for k at least r minus two. At r four and k one, two rank-one projections supported on the first two coordinates of C cubed satisfy the half sandwich relations. Their target is M2 plus C, while the canonical source is M2.
svg.text: A finite extension sees two central parts
f ∈ Aₖ₋₁′; z of f in Aₖ₋₁′ = 1
fxf = Eₖ(x)f; old algebra and Jones projection preserved
Complement: Bs = ℂs; every projection is zero there
When does Aₖ₊₁ map onto B?
k ≤ r−4: new scalar frontier exists; map always exists
s = 0 kills that frontier; s ≠ 0 preserves it
k = r−3: frontier disappears; map exists iff s = 0
k ≥ r−2: old join is already 1; s = 0 automatically
f projects onto (1,1,0)/√2; s projects onto (0,0,1)
A₀′ = M₃: f has full central support
Canonical source M₂; target M₂ ⊕ ℂ; no onto map
